intro: Outlook for insurance claims adjusters on Mac comes down to four setups: a signature, a few server rules, reusable templates and saved searches for claim numbers. Signatures and rules sit under Outlook > Settings, and templates sit under the File menu on the current Outlook for Mac. Lazur can point at each one and talk you through it, one click at a time.
tldr: Check your Outlook client first. Legacy Outlook for Mac stops delivering Exchange Online email after the October 2026 cutoff.
Set a default signature for each account under Outlook > Settings > Mail > Signatures.
Rules run top to bottom and stop at the first match by default, so put the most specific rule first.
Save letters you send every day with File > Save As Template. It needs Microsoft 365 and Outlook for Mac 15.35 or later.
Lazur points, explains, dictates and drafts. It does not click buttons or change your settings for you.

blocks.text: Check which Outlook for Mac you run first

Microsoft ships two Outlook for Mac clients, and their menus differ. The current client keeps signatures at Outlook > Settings > Mail > Signatures and rules at Outlook > Settings > Rules. The legacy client uses Outlook > Settings > Email > Signatures and Tools > Rules. If a path in this guide does not match your screen, you are probably on the other client.

Check which one you use before you change anything. If you see a Legacy Outlook toggle in settings, turn it off to move to the current client. If the toggle is missing, update Outlook through Help > Check for Updates or the Apple App Store. Then reopen the app and check the paths again.

blocks.title: Legacy Outlook has an end date
blocks.text: Legacy Outlook for Mac stops delivering email for Exchange Online accounts after the EWS retirement on October 1, 2026. Microsoft ties continued support to your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license. Move before the deadline, not in the middle of a busy claim week.

If your carrier runs Exchange On-Premises, you have more time. Legacy Outlook for Mac keeps working with Exchange On-Premises until October 9, 2029. After support ends, it receives only security updates, with best-effort technical support. Ask your IT team which Exchange you use, because the answer changes your deadline.

Features also depend on build numbers. Signatures, Snooze and categories appear on Microsoft's feature list from Outlook 16.58 or later. The product page lists other version thresholds too, including 16.42 for Current Channel features and macOS 10.14 or later. If a feature in this guide is missing, check your build first.
Set a signature that fits claims mail

A signature should tell the reader who you are in a few short lines. Put your name, title, carrier and a direct phone line in it. Skip the banner image. A long block under every reply pushes your actual message down, and the reader has to scroll to find the claim number.

Set the default for each account. Go to Outlook > Settings > Mail > Signatures, pick the account, and use Set default signature. You can apply the default to new messages, to replies and forwards, or to both. If you have more than one address, each account needs its own default, so set them one at a time.

Insert a signature by hand when you need a different one. Click in the message body, then select Signature on the Ribbon. If you cannot find it, check under the More button, which holds the items that do not fit on the Ribbon. You can also add Signature to the toolbar by customizing it.

items: Create the signature for your claims account, with name, title, carrier and phone.
Choose Set default signature, then pick new messages, replies or both.
Start a new message with ⌘N and confirm the signature loads in the body.

blocks.text: Many adjusters keep a full signature for new messages and a shorter one for replies. Replies are where claim details matter most, so a short version keeps the text in view. Set the reply default to the short one, then insert the full version by hand when a letter needs it.
Rules that route claim email without losing messages

Rules do most of the sorting, and they cause most of the surprises. Outlook for Mac supports only server rules. Microsoft's page says: You can only create server rules in Outlook for Mac. That means the mail server applies the rule, so it still works when your Mac is asleep.

Rules run top to bottom. You can move a rule up or down with the arrows in the list. The setting called Stop processing more rules is on by default, so when several rules match an email, only the first one applies. This is the setting that catches most people.

Here is a worked example. Suppose a rule that flags anything from a body shop domain sits above a rule that moves any email with a claim number in the subject to the Claims folder. A shop email with a claim number matches both. The flag rule runs first and stops processing, so the claim number rule never fires. Move the claim number rule to the top, and the file lands where it belongs.

rows: Most specific, so it wins first

blocks.text: Microsoft's pages name the rules spot differently. The step page says Outlook > Settings > Rules. The feature list files Rules under Preferences, and it says Available (under tools). If one path fails on your screen, try the other name. Then test each new rule on a real claim email before you trust it.
Templates for letters you send every day

Adjusters write the same few letters again and again. An acknowledgment of claim, a request for photos and a request for a police report are common examples. Write each one once, then save it as a template. You change the claim details and send. Less retyping means fewer wrong claim numbers.

Built-in templates need a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac version 15.35 (170610) or later. Save a message with File > Save As Template. Reuse it with File > New > Mail From Template. The steps are short, but the names matter, so pick names that describe the letter.

items: Write the letter with placeholders in square brackets, such as [claim number].
Choose File > Save As Template, and name it for the letter, such as Photo request.
Choose File > New > Mail From Template when you need it, and pick the template.
Fill every bracket, check the subject line, then send.

blocks.text: Microsoft's template page does not say whether editing a template updates the saved copy. Test that on one template before you rely on it. Change the text, reopen the template, and check the result.

blocks.title: Shared inboxes and My Templates
blocks.text: The My Templates add-in (New Mail ribbon > My Templates > +Template) works only with Microsoft Exchange accounts. It is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac, and your organization can turn add-ins off. If your claims team shares one inbox, ask IT which template option works there.
Search for a claim number across the mailbox

Search for the claim number, not the policyholder's name. The number appears in the subject line, the attachments and the replies on the same file. Names change spelling, and two people can share one name. A claim number is the one thing that ties the thread together.

Outlook for Mac lists several search tools as available. Expanded mail search, offline search, saved searches (smart folders), unified inbox search and search calendar are all on the feature list. Saved searches help most. Save a search for each open claim number, and the results stay one click away when the insured calls back. Search across all items, notes search and tasks search are still under investigation, so do not plan around them.
Share a claims inbox without mixing up replies

Many claims teams share one inbox. Outlook for Mac lists shared and delegate mailboxes as available in Mail. It also lists a Favorite shared mailbox option, plus shared and delegated calendars. Exchange on-premises shared mailbox support is listed as coming soon, so check that if your mailbox sits on-premises.

Shared mailboxes change how rules and templates behave. Rules set on a shared inbox affect everyone who reads it, so give each rule a name that says who owns it and why. Templates are a separate catch, because My Templates does not run in shared mailboxes at all. Plan your letters around that before the team depends on them.
Follow up with Snooze and categories

Snooze hides an email until you choose to see it again. Use it for any file waiting on a vendor, a policyholder or a reinspection. The feature list shows Snooze as available. Snooze keeps the inbox short, but it does not replace a diary. Write the follow-up date on the claim file too.

Categories let you sort by claim status. Microsoft lists Set and manage categories as available in Outlook 16.58 and later. Use one category for each status, such as waiting on photos, waiting on estimate or ready to pay. Keep the list short. A long list goes unused.
Dictate replies and handle claim data carefully

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation works in the reply window, so you can talk through a letter instead of typing it. Add tow yard names, vendor names and model numbers to the personal dictionary, so speech recognition spells them right the first time.

Claim files hold personal and medical details, so treat privacy as part of the workflow. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is not used to train AI models. Your carrier may still limit which AI tools you can use with claim data, so check that policy before you ask about a file.
Common mistakes adjusters make in Outlook for Mac

items: Building a rule without checking the rules above it, so a broad rule swallows claim mail.
Saving a template with real claim details still in it, then sending it to the wrong insured.
Staying on legacy Outlook after the October 2026 cutoff, then wondering why Exchange Online mail stops.
Using a long signature on every reply, so the claim number sits far down the screen.
Searching by policyholder name instead of claim number, and missing part of the thread.
Expecting Lazur to change settings. It points and guides. You click.

blocks.text: A worked example: one hail claim, start to finish

A policyholder emails photos from a hail claim. The subject line has the claim number. Your claim number rule moves the email to the Claims folder. The body shop estimate arrives later with the same number, and the vendor rule moves it to the Vendors folder. Both sit in the file without you sorting them by hand.

You reply from your photo request template, dictate one line about the next inspection, and snooze the file until the shop finishes the estimate. A category marks the file as waiting on estimate. A saved search for the claim number shows the full thread later. Nothing depends on memory, so a colleague can pick up the file quickly.
How Lazur helps while you work in Outlook

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold Option and Command together to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a button is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook. Use it like a colleague who knows the menus, and keep your hand on the mouse.

Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use it for background work, such as checking a recall notice for a vehicle, while you keep working in Outlook. For everyday actions, Lazur can set timers, add Apple Reminders and Calendar events, and open apps and links by voice.
What to do next

Start with the version check, then set one signature and one rule. After that, save two or three templates for your most common letters. Read the [Outlook assistant page](/apps/outlook) for how Lazur handles each screen, or the [insurance agents Outlook guide](/for/insurance-agents/outlook) for a related set of templates and signatures. When you want to try the hold to ask shortcut, [download Lazur](/download) for Mac.
Where the evidence is thin

I did not find a study of how claims adjusters use Outlook for Mac. The one hard number here comes from O*NET, which describes the work, not the software. O*NET lists e-mail as an activity claims adjusters do every day, with 100% of them using it, under code 13-1031.01. O*NET marks that code as retired in favor of 13-1031.00, so read the figure as a strong signal, not proof.

This guide also does not cover Microsoft's known issues with sync and search, because those pages were not checked. If search returns no results, check the Microsoft known issues page for your build before you change anything else.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur works alongside Outlook. It sees your screen only while you hold the shortcut, points at buttons, explains menus and answers out loud. It does not click buttons or operate Outlook for you, and it is not an add-in.

faq.question: Is legacy Outlook for Mac still supported?
faq.answer: Support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026. After the EWS retirement on October 1, 2026, it stops delivering email for Exchange Online accounts. Turn off the Legacy Outlook toggle to switch. If the toggle is missing, update through Help > Check for Updates.

faq.question: Why do my rules skip emails I expected them to catch?
faq.answer: Rules run top to bottom, and Stop processing more rules is on by default. The first match wins, so later rules never run on that email. Move the most specific rule to the top, or turn off the stop setting for rules that should run together.

faq.question: Can I use My Templates on a shared claims mailbox?
faq.answer: Not in Outlook for Mac. The My Templates add-in works only with Microsoft Exchange accounts and is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. Your organization can also turn add-ins off, so ask IT about the built-in option.

faq.question: Which Microsoft subscription do I need for Save As Template?
faq.answer: Built-in templates need a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac version 15.35 (170610) or later. Save a message with File > Save As Template, then reuse it with File > New > Mail From Template.

faq.question: Where do signatures live in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: On the current client, go to Outlook > Settings > Mail > Signatures. Legacy Outlook uses Outlook > Settings > Email > Signatures. Set the default for each account, and choose new messages, replies, forwards or a mix.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe to use with claim files that hold personal data?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is not used to train AI models. Check your carrier's policy on AI tools before you use it with claim files.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, explains, answers out loud, dictates and drafts text. When you ask how to do something, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click before it continues.
